dental-veneers-london.meta_description: Get dental veneers at an award winning, professional, modern dental clinic in Chelsea. Call 020 7148 7148 or book online.

sections.heading: Porcelain Dental Veneers in London, Chelsea
sections.content: Book Online Get dental porcelain veneers in London at the award winning, professional, dental clinic in Chelsea . Our porcelain veneers are made to guarantee beautiful results. Hiding all manner of imperfections and giving your mouth the equivalent of a face-lift.

sections.heading: What Are Veneers?
sections.content: Cosmetic dental veneers are ultra-thin shells of enamel like porcelain that are handcrafted by expert dental ceramists. Ultra-thin veneers are permanently bonded to the front of the teeth. Veneers can cover severely discoloured, poorly shaped or slightly crooked, chipped or worn teeth and make them look amazing. Veneers are used to correct uneven spaces or gaps, or to lighten front teeth that are naturally yellow or grey which can’t be whitened by bleaching.

sections.heading: Before & After
sections.content: Veneers can be used to correct congenital malformations such as peg shaped lateral incisors and retained baby teeth. With our beautifully made porcelain veneers we can correct the shape of teeth and disguise baby teeth into adult teeth. These smile transformations have been life changing for our patients.

sections.heading: The Veneer Procedure
sections.content: The London dental veneer procedure can be completed in two dental visits over the course of 2 weeks. The visits to our dental veneers clinic are comprehensive and can require several hours of examination and tooth preparation. We work with you to select the best tooth colour or maybe a number of shades for extra detail and harmony. As a part of this process, we occasionally recommend teeth whitening before you begin the porcelain veneer treatment to achieve the best results. Based on diagnostic wax-up models, we will determine dimensions of London porcelain veneers that will suit your face and then we advise how much tooth structure needs to be altered if any. Whenever possible, we opt for prepless veneers to preserve your tooth structure. We then take an impression or digital scan of your teeth from which a model of your mouth will be made. We also take numerous digital photos to communicate to the master ceramist the desired results.

sections.heading: Before & After
sections.content: 10 ultra-thin porcelain veneers to improve the inward angle of the teeth and to improve the overall size and colour of the teeth. These veneers were made 0.3 mm thick. Theres no need to damage your teeth in order to have veneers. No tooth reduction necessary in many cases.

sections.heading: Reasons to get dental veneers
sections.content: Considering a smile upgrade? Here are the top reasons to choose dental veneers for a brighter, confident look.

sections.heading: Improve stained teeth
sections.content: Over time, natural teeth can become discoloured due to factors like coffee, red wine, tobacco, and certain medications. While teeth whitening treatments can address some of these stains, they might not always achieve the desired results. Veneers, with their thin porcelain shells are custom-made to fit over the front surface of your teeth, presenting a bright and natural appearance. Not only do they mask stubborn stains, but they also resist future discoloration, ensuring a consistently radiant smile.

sections.heading: Improve chipped or damaged teeth
sections.content: Veneers are a game-changer for those with chipped or damaged teeth. Accidents, wear, or even biting into hard foods can lead to unsightly chips or damage. When affixed to the front surface of the affected tooth, a veneer seamlessly blends in, restoring the tooth’s natural shape and appearance. Beyond just aesthetics, veneers provide a protective shield, preventing further damage or wear.

sections.heading: Gain self-confidence
sections.content: Veneers can be transformative not just for one’s smile, but also for their self-confidence. A radiant, flawless smile often translates to increased self-assuredness in social, professional, and personal settings. Imperfections like stains, gaps, or misalignments, no matter how minor, can sometimes make individuals self-conscious or hesitant to smile freely. Veneers address these concerns by offering a custom-made, natural-looking solution that revitalises one’s appearance.

sections.heading: Before & After
sections.content: 10 veneers to improve the size of the teeth and the spaces between the teeth. No anaesthetic. No drilling. No tooth reduction. Not only were the teeth not touched prior to having veneers but the veneers will in fact provide extra strength and support to the teeth.

sections.heading: How long do veneers last?
sections.content: Porcelain dental veneers typically grace your smile for a remarkable 10 to 20 years. With their stellar durability and resistance to everyday stains, dental veneers are a favourite for those seeking a lasting transformation. To keep them shining, simply maintain regular dental hygiene, be mindful of hard foods, and pop in for routine dental visits.

sections.heading: What are temporary veneers?
sections.content: Since there is an approximately two week period to fabricate the ceramic veneers, temporary veneers are fabricated and fitted. The temporaries will give you a preview of the expected outcome and also help us identify adjustments that may be needed during the fabrication of the permanent tooth porcelain veneers.

sections.heading: Do veneers damage your teeth?
sections.content: Veneers do not damage your teeth if the teeth are not cut down extensively as for crowns. If the teeth are already in a good position to receive veneers then they may not need any filing down or cutting. In these ideal cases, veneers can simply be placed over the top of the teeth. In some cases veneers can even be protective if the tooth underneath is worn or damaged. In the past, adhesives were not as strong as they are today and teeth were cut down to a peg and a cap/crown was made over the top. Now, adhesives are so strong that veneers can be made to cover just the front surface of the tooth. Veneers can now be made as thin as 0.3-0.5 mm. In some cases the tooth does not need any filing or reduction as there is sufficient space for the veneer to cover it.

sections.heading: Can you eat and brush normally with veneers?
sections.content: You can eat normally with veneers. It is advised to avoid biting into hard foods especially any biting motion that may act as a lever. We would suggest to avoid biting into items such as apples, chocolate bars and crusty rolls for example. Veneers do not break or fall off if you are careful with them and if they have been put on by an experienced dentist.

sections.heading: Will veneers stain and can I whiten them?
sections.content: Porcelain/ceramic veneers do not stain as they have a shiny smooth surface. Composite veneers on the other hand are more prone to staining. Veneers can not be whitened. It is therefore necessary to make sure you choose a colour that you will be happy with long term.

sections.heading: How much do veneers cost in London?
sections.content: Ceramic veneers will vary in price depending on the dentist and the technician who makes the veneers. Well made ceramic veneers will generally cost £750-£1200 for each tooth. This will include all the appointments, preparation and fitting. An individual veneer may sometimes be more expensive than a set of veneers as it is harder for the dentist and technician to match an individual veneer to the neighbouring teeth. Before the veneers are actually made you will most likely need to have a diagnostic mock up of the end result. This will also cost around £500 for one arch to be mocked up.

sections.heading: What type of veneer is best?
sections.content: There are two main types of veneer; eMax and empress. The dentist will be the best person to advise you on which would be better for you. EMax veneers are stronger and will be less likely to chip or break. Empress veneers may be more natural looking but will not be as strong as Emax.

sections.heading: What is the procedure for veneers?
sections.content: For veneers you would normally need 3 appointments. The first appointment is the consultation to discuss what you want and impressions to create a model of the desired end result. The second appointment is to make any necessary preparations to the teeth and take impressions of the teeth for construction of the final veneers. At this appointment temporary veneers of the end result will also be made. At the third appointment the veneers will be bonded to your teeth and you will have your beautiful smile.

sections.heading: Before & After
sections.content: We make our porcelain veneers with multiple layers of different ceramics to emulate a natural tooth as closely as possible. We include natural characteristics that exist in a natural tooth and we allow light reflections from all the correct angles to give you the most natural looking veneers that can be made.

sections.heading: Dentures In Chelsea, London
sections.content: Book Online Dentures are available at our dental clinic in Chelsea, London and Reigate in Surrey . They are a removable set of artificial teeth – either complete or partial – made to replace natural teeth you have lost, and are used to restore appearance and oral functions.

sections.heading: Custom made bespoke cosmetic Dentures
sections.content: Dentures are more comfortable and natural looking than ever before and, unless you tell someone that you’re wearing dentures, they probably won’t even know. Once made and fitted, these custom-made replacements are easily put in and taken out of your mouth by you, giving you the flexibility to wear them at times that suit you. We custom make dentures based on impressions and measurements taken of your mouth. This approach guarantees you a set of dentures that fit comfortably, give you a proper bite, and look like your natural teeth did. Complete dentures are used when all teeth need replacing on your upper jaw, lower jaw, or both. Partial dentures are used when some natural teeth remain, and fit in amongst and around those remaining teeth. Complete dentures are held in place with a gum coloured acrylic base that fits snugly over your gums. Partial dentures rest on a framework that attaches to your remaining teeth. Alternatives to partial dentures are bridges and implants . We can advise on the recommended course of action after assessing your teeth and your preferences.

sections.heading: Visit our Dental Clinic in Chelsea or Reigate
sections.content: Several visits to our dental clinic will be required for the fitting of and checking up of your dentures. Due to normal wear and tear, and also because, as you age, your mouth shape will naturally alter, realignments and replacements will be required may be required after 5 years. 12 month return visits are recommended. Whilst developments in dentures have made them more comfortable than previously, they won’t feel exactly the same as natural teeth, and will take some getting used to. Eating and speaking with dentures may feel awkward for the first few weeks, but over time you’ll adjust to them and will be able to eat and speak as normal.

sections.heading: HIghest quality Dentures
sections.content: Looking after the highg quality dentures is straightforward. The key things to do are to always handle them with care, to clean them daily, and to leave them to soak when not in use. They can be worn all day and night if required, however, taking them out at night is advisable.

sections.heading: Dermal Fillers in London
sections.content: Book Online Experience professional dermal fillers and lip fillers at an award-winning clinic in Chelsea, London. Our modern facility is known for delivering exceptional care and results in cosmetic treatments.

sections.heading: Which dermal filler should I choose ?
sections.content: There are many different types of dermal fillers and many different brands. At The Wellington Clinic we only use the top brands which have undergone many years of testing and research. We mainly work with the TEOXANE TEOSYAL and JUVÉDERM® VYCROSS ranges for the outstanding properties that they hold. Most types of dermal filler are composed of Hyaluronic acid. Hyaluronic acid naturally exists within the skin giving volume, shape, hydration and elasticity. Hyaluronic acid has minimal risk of reactions and is more readily accepted by the body than other silicone or collagen fillers.

sections.heading: What happens during the procedure ?
sections.content: For certain dermal filler procedures topical anaesthetic is first applied and left to numb the skin for 20-30 minutes. A numbing injection can be given to numb the area further although this is rarely required. The dermal filler is then injected into the area required using a very fine needle or blunt ended cannula. Results can be seen immediately after dermal filler treatments and generally last up to 12 months or longer.

sections.heading: Lip Fillers London
sections.content: Dr Marjan Goodacre offers some of the best lip fillers and she takes the utmost care when treating the lips. When applying our lip fillers in London, she takes all factors into account to enhance each individual aspect of the lips some of which are described below. Read more about our different lip fillers in London below.

sections.heading: Lip Border
sections.content: If your lips are not as defined as they used to be, border line lip fillers can be used to enhance the definition and outline of your lips. This London lip filler treatment is also ideal for anyone who is developing lip lines (also known as smokers lines or barcode lines). Lip lines develop as volume is lost in our lips and in the tissues around our lips. Lip lines can be frustrating as they cause lipstick to bleed. More importantly lip lines change the shape of the lips, ageing the entire face and can even cause further creasing and loss of volume around the lips.

sections.heading: Lip Body
sections.content: If you love the shape of your lips and simply want to add volume, lip body enhancement can be done for you. Lip body treatments can be used for a subtle enhancement or a noticeable change. If you want a subtle enhancement it will simply make your lips feel and look healthier and more hydrated. If however you want a noticeable change in volume this can also be done with Lip Body Treatments. The placement of filler is positioned accurately to maintain the natural feel and movement of your lips. This technique ensures a natural appearance of your new enhanced lips.

sections.heading: Cupid Bow Lips
sections.content: The Cupid Bow is the V-shape contour in the centre of the upper lip that forms the 2 peaks and bow shaped upper lip. Cupid Bow Lip Filler Treatments can be used to enhance the Cupid Bow to create more curvature and shape of the upper lip. This lip filler in London will help contour the lips if you don’t like your flat upper lip. If you would like to further enhance your Cupid Bow then you may require the additional support of the Philtrum Column filler treatment.

sections.heading: Philtrum Column
sections.content: The Philtrum Columns are the raised vertical columns that extend from the peaks of the upper lip to the nose. Some people have very well-defined natural Philtrum columns and others have an entirely flat area above the lip with no column shape. If you would like to enhance the shape of your Philtrum Columns this treatment is for you. There are different reasons for having Philtrum Column Filler Treatment other than creating the Column contouring you may be fond of. Creating a Philtrum Column will add curve and contouring to the area above the upper lip. As we age the area above the upper lip flattens and lengthens and so this treatment is ideal to bring back the youthful curvy and well supported upper lip area. If you feel the area above your upper lip is too long this treatment can also help to create the youthful curves, structure and support which will also help to make this area appear shorter and better supported. If you feel the border of your upper lip is too flat and you would like to enhance the Cupid Bow appearance further this treatment will help support the Cupid Bow enhancement and add further curvature of the upper lip.

sections.heading: Lower Face Filler Treatments
sections.content: These treatments are important to consider if you want to improve your lips. The skin surrounding the lips are essential in providing strength and support for the lips. Therefore when these surrounding tissues are treated correctly, the final lip appearance is enhanced as well as enhancing the lower half of the face.

sections.heading: Upper Face Fillers
sections.content: Dr Marjan Goodacre offers some of the best lip fillers and she takes the utmost care when treating the lips. When applying our lip fillers in London, she takes all factors into account to enhance each individual aspect of the lips some of which are described below. Read more about our different lip fillers in London below.

sections.heading: Cheek augmentation
sections.content: This is a highly effective treatment not only to enhance the cheek bones but also to lift the skin and reduce facial lines and sagging. Cheek fillers can be used to create better facial structures and support. For women wanting a high cheek bone or better definition of their faces this treatment can create beautiful results. For men who want a more structured face, cheek augmentation can help to create that. If you are happy with the shapes of your cheeks but would instead like to have a mini face lift, this can also be done. Cheek augmentation can be used to simply lift the skin and reduce the heaviness that develops around the mouth and cheeks. Smile line filler is also a perfect way to reduce smile lines and to stop them from getting worse. Cheek augmentation is also good to help reduce a tired facial appearance and to reduce a dark or hollow under eye area.

sections.heading: Tear trough filler
sections.content: This treatment is perfect for those with tired looking eyes, dark circles, hollows or deep grooves below your eyes. This treatment also helps support the delicate skin below the eyes.

sections.heading: Nose filler
sections.content: Nose reshaping, also known as non-surgical rhinoplasty, is great for those who want to avoid nose surgery. Nose filler in London can help to align the nose or improve a hump on the nose or create a better defined ridge.

sections.heading: Temple filler
sections.content: These treatments are ideal for those with hollow temples on the sides of their heads. This treatment is not only useful to improve the hollows but to also support and lift the skin from lower down.

sections.heading: Brow filler
sections.content: These treatments are great to help lift the brows where they will have dropped down over the years. This treatment restores the shape of the bone beneath the brow creating a better supported eyebrow.

sections.heading: Forehead filler
sections.content: These treatments are great to improve stubborn lines and creases or to restore the curve back into the forehead. As we age the forehead will flatten and lengthen. This treatment helps to minimise the effects of forehead ageing.

sections.heading: Lower Face Fillers
sections.content: There are a number of changes that occur in the skin around the mouth which in turn cause different lines and creases to develop. Some of the lines that develop around the mouth are only evident during movement of the facial muscles whereas others can be present even when the face is motionless. The appearance of these lines can be reduced and improved with the use of lower face filler treatments which also provide better support to lips. Treatment options include lip lines filler, nasolabial smile lines filler, marionette lines filler, mental lines filler, and other smile lines filler treatments. Other treatments that provide better support for the lower face and lips are chin and jaw enhancements which help to provide structure and support to the lower part of the face and to tighten saggy skin.

sections.heading: Nasolabial smile lines
sections.content: These smile lines extend from the corner of the nose almost to the corner of the mouth. The biggest deficiency that develops for some people is at the corner of the tip of the nose making a shadow in these areas. For others the nasolabial lines are most severe on smiling but when they begin to be visible at rest it is a good time to start addressing them.

sections.heading: Marionette lines
sections.content: These lines extend from the corners of the mouth downwards and can contribute to a downward smile giving a saddened appearance. Marionette lines can also occasionally be so severe that the corners of the mouth get sore all the time from saliva collecting there. Strengthening of the marionette lines with dermal filler provides better shape and support of the lips and also the lower face.

sections.heading: Mental crease
sections.content: This filler treatment is for the horizontal line between the lower lip and the chin. This area is smooth and flat when we are young but can get deeper with age and gradually forms a crease. Dermal filler can help to not only remove lines in this area but to also provide the structure and support required for the lips and lower half of the face.

sections.heading: Chin filler
sections.content: These treatments are used to treat a variety of issues around the chin area. If you feel your chin is too pointy or even too pronounced we can help to recontour the areas around the chin and create a chin that is more harmonious with the face and less obtrusive. If you feel your chin is set back and your profile could do with improving then we can bring your chin forward to create the ideal facial profile. If your face is too round or your lower face is too short we can create a longer, more youthful face for you. If you don’t like your chin dimples and creases we can erase them for you. If the skin texture over your chin is not as supple and smooth as it used to be, the chin filler treatments can also help to resolve these issues. If you have a double chin effect or saggy skin around your jawline, chin augmentation along with jawline augmentation could help you.

sections.heading: Jaw line
sections.content: Jawline augmentation is a great treatment that is used to not only define the jaw line but to help pin back any loose saggy skin. Jawline augmentation can help to change the contours of the jaw to change the lower face shape. For women, it is great to create a more uplifting jaw and better defined jaws reducing saggy skin. For men, jaw augmentation can be used to reduce saggy skin or if required to create a more masculine jaw.

sections.heading: Non-Surgical Rhinoplasty/Nose Job
sections.content: Non-surgical rhinoplasty, also known as the 15 minute nose job, is an excellent procedure for anyone wanting to improve the shape of their nose without the trauma, expense and downtime of surgery. Marjan Goodacre has been through specialist training for non-surgical rhinoplasty / nose job procedures and provides these treatments to many patients who are concerned about the appearance of their nose. With non-surgical rhinoplasty, Dr Marjan Goodacre uses dermal filler to correct the alignment of the nose, to reduce the hump, to improve a flat nose and create a ridge, to correct a downward nose or to simply refine the appearance of the nose. Non-surgical rhinoplasty is a very simple procedure with immediate results that last for 12 months.

sections.heading: Tear Trough
sections.content: This treatment is a highly sought after treatment as it improves the appearance under the eye immediately making you look brighter, fresh and less tired looking. Tear trough filler treatments help improve dark circles and deep grooves or hollows and it even helps improve the wrinkles under the eye area too. Dr Marjan Goodacre provides tear trough treatments using a fine tip called a blunt cannula and so reducing the risks associated with a needle near the delicate eye area. With Dr Marjan Goodacre’s gentle technique there is only one insertion point in the skin and so there is minimal trauma and downtime involved and you get to enjoy the results immediately.

sections.heading: Chin and Jawline
sections.content: These treatments are used to treat a variety of issues around the chin area. If you feel your chin is too pointy or even too pronounced, Dr Marjan Goodacre can help to recontour the areas around the chin and create a chin that is more harmonious with the face and less obtrusive.

sections.heading: Chin filler
sections.content: These treatments are used to treat a variety of issues around the chin area. If you feel your chin is too pointy or even too pronounced, Dr Marjan Goodacre can help to recontour the areas around the chin and create a chin that is more harmonious with the face and less obtrusive. If you feel your chin is set back and your profile could do with improving then she can bring your chin forward to create the ideal facial profile. If your face is too round or your lower face is too short she can create a longer, more youthful face for you. If you don’t like your chin dimples and creases she can erase them for you. If the skin texture over your chin is not as supple and smooth as it used to be, the chin filler treatments can also help to resolve these issues. If you have a double chin effect or saggy skin around your jawline, chin augmentation along with jawline augmentation could help you.

sections.heading: Jawline augmentation
sections.content: This is a great treatment that is used to not only define the jawline but to help pin back any loose saggy skin. Jawline augmentation can help to change the contours of the jaw to change the lower face shape. For women, it is great to create a more uplifting jaw and better defined jaws reducing saggy skin and even improving the double chin. For men, jaw augmentation can be used to reduce saggy skin or if required to create a more masculine jaw. Dr Marjan Goodacre can help improve your lower half face with her chin and jaw line treatment techniques.

sections.heading: Non-Surgical Face Lift
sections.content: If you feel you could do with a mini-facelift but don’t want to go through the trauma, expense and downtime then book an appointment with Dr Marjan Goodacre. She can create the same results and give you immediate results with minimum downtime and expense. Dr Marjan Goodacre uses aspects of the 8-point face lift and MD Codes to provide her own bespoke mini face lift, creating beauty in proportions and in harmony with the rest of the face. A treatment plan will be created specifically for you to obtain maximum results. The results are natural and not obtrusively obvious. Our patients normally hear comments like “you look so well” but no-one can tell what they have had done. It’s an outstanding treatment with outstanding results and minimal downtime.

sections.heading: Which parts of the face should I treat with dermal filler?
sections.content: Dermal fillers can be used to treat different areas of the face, including the lips, chin, jaw, cheeks, forehead and nose, and are ideal for dealing with specific issues such as loss of volume, deep lines, tear troughs, and jowls. The different treatment types are explained in detail below and prices can be found on the Face Prices page . Some methods are more appropriate for some people than others. Dr Marjan Goodacre takes care to assess this and discuss it with you. Book in for a full face and skin assessment and consultation.

sections.heading: What do dermal fillers involve?
sections.content: This cosmetic procedure typically involves the injection of hyaluronic acid to add volume to tissue and fill wrinkles. Some areas which we can inject with fillers include: The skin around the eye Cheeks Mouth and jawline Tissue around the lips

sections.heading: What are dermal fillers made of?
sections.content: Dermal fillers can be either collagen, calcium hydroxyl or hyaluronic acid. In the past collagen fillers were used which caused reactions in some people and so are no longer used. Some fillers are made of calcium hydroxyl apatite but can not be dissolved if needed to be removed for any reason. Most fillers are now made of hyaluronic acid which naturally exists in the skin so there are no risk of allergies. Hyaluronic acid fillers produce the most natural results and are the safest as they can be dissolved if needed.

sections.heading: How long do fillers last?
sections.content: Each brand and make of filler can last a different length of time. Some last around 6 months and others can last 12 to 18 months. The part of the face the filler was placed in can also affect how long it lasts. Filler can wear off more quickly in mobile areas like the lips. Filler that is more dense like those used for cheekbones or for the jawline will also last longer.

sections.heading: What types of dermal fillers do you offer?
sections.content: We offer a wide range of dermal fillers – from lip fillers, to upper and lower face fillers and tear troughs. We also provide fillers for ear lobes and hands. Read our Dermal Fillers in London Treatment Areas above and look at the price list for the full list.

sections.heading: Is dermal filler safe?
sections.content: Dermal fillers are safe when the necessary precautions have been taken. It is important to use a hyaluronic acid filler that can be dissolved if required. Collagen and hydroxylapatite fillers can not be dissolved and so if they block a vessel there is no easy way of unblocking the vessel. It is important to use an FDA approved filler like Juvederm that has been through rigorous testing and clinical trials to approve its use as safe and effective.

sections.heading: Is there any downtime for dermal fillers?
sections.content: If you encounter any particular symptoms, please feel free to give us a call. Usually, there’s minimal downtime for a dermal filler but you should expect potential swelling and bruising, in some cases.

sections.heading: Do dermal fillers hurt?
sections.content: Dermal fillers are not surgical procedures, and therefore do not require any cuts, incisions or stitches. You may feel discomfort as the fillers are injected, but our facial aesthetician specialist will go as slowly as you like. Many describe the feeling of a dermal filler to be like a tiny scratch, and it typically takes no more than 20 – 30 minutes. If you are feeling concerned, we can apply some local anaesthetic to the area.

sections.heading: How much do fillers cost?
sections.content: The cost of dermal fillers will mainly depend on the type of product that is used. Some filler brands are much cheaper than others. This may be because they are not FDA approved or they do not last very long. Most clinics will charge based on the amount of filler that is used. Most syringes of filler are 1ml and prices will correspond to that amount. Some clinics may charge based on the area you are having treated but you may end up paying more than the amount you needed. The cost of dermal fillers may then be further dependent on the clinic and the clinician. A CQC registered clinic with all the systems and protocols in place to ensure safe and sterile treatments may charge more than a beauty room with slightly different facilities. A dentist or doctor will also be charging more than a beautician who should not really be carrying out these procedures. The Juvederm Vycross range for example will cost around £400. Juvederm Ultra range which doesn’t last as long may be £300.

sections.heading: How Dermaroller Works
sections.content: Microneedling is also known as collagen induction therapy (CIT). The dermaroller/Dermastamp treatment technique involves creating microscopic channels through the skin, which in turn activate the body’s natural healing cycle. This activation causes the formation of collagen in the skin. The skin contains 75% collagen. The collagen provides support for skin and is responsible for the smooth, plump, healthy-looking skin that exists at a young age. As the skin ages, the amount of collagen decreases, and so the support for our skin diminishes, resulting in thin, unsupported, wrinkled skin.

sections.heading: Is microneedling safe?
sections.content: The treatment might sound scary, but it is very safe when handled by a professional. Our microneedling Chelsea clinic offers a safe and secure environment for your microneedling treatment. For safe and professional microneedling in Chelsea, book your appointment at The Wellington Clinic today. We offer skilled aestheticians who are trained in this specialist and minimally invasive procedure. After your dermaroller facial treatment, you might have some minor redness and irritation on your skin for a few days. This should subside and should not be too uncomfortable.

sections.heading: What results can I expect after Dermaroller/Dermastamp?
sections.content: Dermaroller treatment stimulates collagen production, which in turn produces healthier, younger-looking skin. This type of microneedling treatment is also non-ablative, meaning that the deeper parts of the skin are treated without damaging the top layer of the skin, which happens with laser procedures.

sections.heading: Does Dermaroller work for acne scars?
sections.content: In the case of acne scars, stretch marks or other scars, the initiation of the body’s healing cycle helps the scar tissue to be broken down and the formation of new collagen to improve the skin. Dermaroller acne scar treatment can be very successful for diminishing scars and smoothing the skin. Before treatment, we will assess your skin to determine the type of scarring. Deep acne scars are treated in a different way from shallow acne scars. We will help you to determine the best treatment choice for your skin concerns.

sections.heading: What is the Difference Between Dermaroller & eDS?
sections.content: Dermaroller is a rolling device. This means the needles do not penetrate and exit the skin vertically, and as a result, a wedge shape is made on the skin surface. The needles on an Electric Dermastamp (eDS) move vertically, and as a result, ideal sized micro-channels are created. This allows for Collagen Induction without unnecessarily damaging the epidermis (the uppermost layer of the skin). eDS is ideal for the face where precision of the micro-needling treatment is of the utmost importance to provide optimum results with minimal trauma. eDS also allows for the needle length to be altered easily for different parts of the face. This is important as the needles need to penetrate different depths on the different areas of the face for optimum results.

sections.heading: What is the dermaroller procedure?
sections.content: Topical anaesthetic cream is applied to the area to be treated, and it is left on the skin for 30 min to work. Once the area is numb, the eDS tip is gently passed over the skin while the microfine needles penetrate very smoothly and quickly to the correct skin depth. A skin rejuvenation treatment solution is applied to the face to allow the eDS tip to glide smoothly over the skin and add extra benefits to the skin.

sections.heading: What our are dermaroller solutions?
sections.content: The solutions used are Hyaluronic Acid solution to provide intensive hydration or CIT Mesotherapy solution. In addition to hyaluronic acid, the CIT Mesotherapy solution contains: Vitamin A for skin regeneration Vitamin C and E for antioxidant protection Niacinamide for skin brightening Peptides and amino acids for skin cell stimulation Additional skin-enhancing ingredients Once the entire area is treated, a calming lotion is applied to the skin to soothe the skin, and a mask is then applied to intensively hydrate and soothe the skin. The mask contains: Vitamin E Retinol palmitate Hyaluronic acid Ceramide amytriptil. Sun protection is then applied and given for you to continue using for two weeks after treatment.

sections.heading: What happens after dermaroller treatment?
sections.content: During the six weeks following microneedling treatment, the skin’s natural regeneration occurs, and new collagen and skin cells are formed. The skins blood supply is enhanced, bringing more nutrients, hydration and oxygen to the skin.

sections.heading: How long does dermaroller treatment last?
sections.content: The process allows a natural and long-lasting enhancement and regeneration. Three procedures are typically recommended, with approximately six weeks between them. Once you’ve completed your treatment, you can expect the results to last around six to eight months. After this time, you can arrange regular top-up treatments for microneedling in Chelsea.

sections.heading: How do I know if my tooth infection is serious?
sections.content: A serious tooth infection is often characterised by severe, persistent pain that may radiate to the ear, jaw, or neck. You might also notice swelling in the face, cheek, or around the affected tooth. Accompanying symptoms can include fever, tender swollen lymph nodes under the jaw or in the neck, a bad taste in the mouth, bad breath, and difficulty swallowing or breathing. An untreated infection can spread and lead to severe complications.

sections.heading: What is classed as a dental emergency?
sections.content: A dental emergency is typically recognized by severe pain, bleeding, or immediate risk to the teeth. Examples include knocked-out or loosened teeth from trauma, intense toothaches that hinder daily activities, swelling in the mouth or face suggesting an infection, or persistent bleeding from the mouth. Complications from recent dental surgeries, such as lost stitches or severe post-operative pain, also qualify. Additionally, broken or cracked teeth with pain or sharp edges, as well as lost or damaged fillings, crowns, or bridges causing discomfort, are considered emergencies.

sections.heading: What does a tooth infection feel like?
sections.content: A tooth infection often presents as a throbbing, persistent pain in or around the affected tooth. The pain can sometimes radiate to the jaw, ear, or neck. Sensitivity to hot, cold, or pressure when biting down is common. The area might be tender to touch, and there can be swelling in the nearby gums or face. Some people also experience a foul taste in the mouth or persistent bad breath. In more advanced cases, fever or swollen lymph nodes might be present.

sections.heading: How long can you have a tooth infection before sepsis?
sections.content: The time between a tooth infection and the onset of sepsis can vary widely, from days to weeks, depending on the individual and the severity of the infection. While some infections remain localised, others can spread rapidly. Factors like the person’s immune response, the presence of other health conditions, and the virulence of the bacteria play roles.

sections.heading: What are the signs of dental sepsis?
sections.content: Dental sepsis is a severe infection originating from a tooth and potentially spreading to other body parts. Symptoms often include a severe toothache or pain in the affected region, accompanied by facial, jaw, or neck swelling. Individuals might also experience an elevated body temperature or fever, redness and warmth around the infected area, and a foul taste or persistent bad breath. Dental sepsis can escalate quickly, leading to serious, potentially life-threatening complications if left untreated.

sections.heading: What is an endodontist?
sections.content: An endodontist is a specialist in the field of dentistry who focuses on diseases of the dental pulp and nerves of the teeth. They have completed additional training beyond dental school, typically two to three years, to become experts in performing root canal therapy and diagnosing and treating dental pain. Their advanced skills and techniques, often involving complex surgeries, are used to save natural teeth that might otherwise need to be extracted. In essence, if you have a toothache or suspect you need a root canal, an endodontist is the specialist to see.

sections.heading: Is it better to go to an endodontist for a root canal?
sections.content: Yes, it can be advantageous to visit an endodontist for a root canal. Endodontists are root canal specialists who have undergone additional years of training specifically focused on diagnosing tooth pain and performing root canal treatment and other procedures related to the interior of the tooth. They are skilled in handling complex cases and are proficient with advanced technologies. They perform root canal treatments frequently, so they’re experienced in managing a variety of situations. While general dentists are trained to perform root canals, endodontists specialise in such procedures, increasing your chances of a successful, comfortable treatment and preserving your natural teeth.

sections.heading: How long does a root canal take?
sections.content: The length of a root canal treatment can vary depending on the root canal specialist, complexity of the tooth’s structure and the specific condition of the tooth. Generally, a root canal can be completed in one appointment lasting about 90 minutes. Simple cases might be resolved in a single visit, while more complex cases, such as those involving molars or re-treatments, might require additional time or sessions. After the root canal treatment, a separate appointment is often scheduled for a crown or other restoration to protect the treated tooth and restore it to full function.

sections.heading: Fixed Metal & Ceramic Braces In Chelsea, London
sections.content: Book Online Fixed metal and ceramic dental braces are an orthodontic treatment we offer at our dental clinic on the Kings Road in Chelsea, London.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Also known as ‘train tracks’ or ‘fixed appliances’, fixed braces are the most common type of orthodontic appliance used to correct issues such as crooked teeth, crowded teeth, overbites and underbites. Fixed braces are often recommended by orthodontists for straightening teeth because they produce very precise tooth movements and provide more control over teeth than a removable brace does. They have a long, proven record of achieving accurate results for patients of all ages. A fixed brace consists of small brackets bonded to the front of each your teeth. Each of these brackets acts as a kind of handle on the tooth, which can be used to individually and precisely control it’s positioning. A thin wire connects each of the teeth bonded brackets and applies tension to the brackets to gently move and straighten your teeth over time. They are ‘fixed’ in that once fitted to your teeth, the brackets and wires of the brace will only be removed again by the orthodontist at the end of the treatment plan. This contrasts to removable braces, like Invisalign braces , which you can remove yourself any time. The modern brackets used for a fixed brace are very different to the ones used a decade or more ago, that many adults will remember from their school days. The brackets on today’s braces are smaller, less noticeable and more aesthetically pleasing. An alternative option is lingual braces , which work in a similar manner but where the brackets are bonded to the back of your teeth instead.

sections.heading: Ceramic brackets
sections.content: In addition to the standard stainless steel brackets, which can now be customised with colours, ceramic brackets are available too. Ceramic brackets are the same size and shape as metal ones, but are made to be tooth coloured so as to better blend in with your teeth. Tooth coloured wires are an option too, to make the brace even less noticeable. There are multiple brands of fixed braces available. Whilst they all essentially perform the same function, there are some differences between them and some may be more suitable for you than others. At your appointment, our orthodontist, after examining your teeth, will outline your options and make a recommendation to you that will best suit your needs. It will take about 1-2 hours for your fixed brace to be fitted. It is a painless process though some discomfort may be felt. For the first few days after the fitting, your teeth and jaw may feel uncomfortable whilst your mouth adjusts to the brace, but this will quickly pass. It varies on the severity of the issue and how far your teeth need to be moved, but fixed braces typically take 12-24 months to have their complete effect on fixing your teeth. Throughout this timeframe, you will need to visit the orthodontist at our dental clinic at 6-8 week intervals so that they can make minor adjustments to the brackets and wires of the brace to keep moving your teeth in the right direction. Your speech may be temporarily affected following the fitting of the brace, but this is just a short phase and within a week you should be able to speak clearly and naturally again. Whilst wearing a fixed brace, you’ll be able to eat normally, but should be cautious when eating certain hard foods, like crusty bread and uncut apples. Hard boiled sweets, chewy sweets and chewing gum should be avoided.

sections.heading: Hyperhidrosis Treatment London
sections.content: Book Online We know how much of an impact excessive sweating or hyperhidrosis can have on your daily life

sections.heading: Excessive sweating treatment
sections.content: If you’re suffering from hyperhidrosis and it’s taking a toll on your mental health, we can help you live a normal life with botox treatment injections for hyperhidrosis. If your condition hasn’t improved with self-help treatments, then medical hyperhidrosis treatment at The Wellington Clinic could be a treatment worth considering.

sections.heading: What is hyperhidrosis?
sections.content: Hyperhidrosis is a condition otherwise known as excessive sweating. It can affect the whole body or it can affect only isolated areas. If you suffer from this condition, you’re more likely to find that you���re excessively sweating from places on your body that have a high concentration of sweat glands. These include areas such as the hands, feet, armpit and groin area. While it’s normal to sweat during physical activity or if you get hot, if you find that you’re sweating without doing any physical activity or when your body does not need to be cooled down – you may be suffering from hyperhidrosis.

sections.heading: Is hyperhidrosis a common problem?
sections.content: Hyperhidrosis affects roughly around 2-3% of the population, and it is a relatively common problem. However, only 40% of those who have the condition are likely to seek treatment. Hyperhidrosis can be difficult to live with, but luckily, it can be easily treated. The treatment will depend on the severity of your hyperhidrosis and where it presents on the body. Treatments can include: Tablets Botox injections Iontophoresis treatment Sweat gland surgery At The Wellington Clinic, we offer botox injections to treat hyperhidrosis, in addition to being a top dental clinic in Chelsea .

sections.heading: How many types of hyperhidrosis are there?
sections.content: Primary hyperhidrosis affects smaller areas of the body with excessive sweating, while secondary hyperhidrosis affects the entire body and is caused secondary to something else. While primary hyperhidrosis often occurs for no apparent reason, secondary hyperhidrosis may occur due to certain medical conditions or as a side effect of certain medication.

sections.heading: What causes hyperhidrosis?
sections.content: There’s a wide range of causes and triggers of hyperhidrosis. Here are a few examples below:

sections.heading: What are some self-help treatments for hyperhidrosis?
sections.content: Self-help treatments such as applying a topical powder such as talcum powder can help absorb excess sweat. Unfortunately, these topical powders can only help in mild cases. Another self-care option is to use stronger antiperspirants containing aluminium chloride on the hands, feet and armpits. These are applied at night and washed off in the morning 2-3 times a week. These antiperspirants can cause skin irritation over time. In case this happens, you should consult your doctor.

sections.heading: Botox treatment for excessive sweating
sections.content: Before we begin treating hyperhidrosis, we’ll first identify and mark out the area so we can target the right areas. Treatment will involve injecting a small amount of botox into the skin targeting your sweat glands. This will stop your sweat glands from producing sweat. The treatment involves a number of small injections made in the affected area. We can provide you with numbing cream before the treatment to make the procedure comfortable and easy for you. Your skin may be a little red and inflamed after treatment but this settles very quickly. The treatment will last several months and the effects will gradually wear off.

sections.heading: What is the downtime of the treatment?
sections.content: There aren’t typically many side effects associated with this treatment. You might have some bruising or tenderness at the injected area although this is uncommon.

sections.heading: How long will it take to see the effects of the treatment?
sections.content: Many of our patients see improvements in the first week of treatment but you will see the full effects at 2 weeks after treatment. You can expect the treatment to last between 3-6 months.

sections.heading: Why do people need this treatment?
sections.content: Many people who suffer from hyperhidrosis need treatment. They have it for multiple reasons including: It’s a quick solution to what can be a long-term problem Highly effective treatment against hyperhidrosis Reduces moisture in the skin and skin is left dry Keeps symptoms under control Improves self-confidence and self-esteem Reduces anxiety and stress

sections.heading: Is hyperhidrosis genetic?
sections.content: Hyperhidrosis is a common condition that affects around 3% of the population. There is no conclusive evidence that hyperhidrosis is a genetic condition.

sections.heading: Is hyperhidrosis dangerous?
sections.content: In itself, hyperhidrosis isn’t a dangerous condition, and there isn’t an established link between excessive sweating and dehydration. However, hyperhidrosis can have a significant and negative impact on your self-esteem and wellbeing.

sections.heading: Will hyperhidrosis go away on its own?
sections.content: Occasionally, hyperhidrosis does get better with age – but be aware that this is rather rare. Many people actually notice that their hyperhidrosis gets worse with age. As time passes, hyperhidrosis could go on to affect other areas of the body. The only real way to get relief from hyperhidrosis is to seek help from a doctor or a dermatologist.

sections.heading: Will my hyperhidrosis treatment be permanent?
sections.content: If you undergo surgery for your hyperhidrosis treatment, the results will be permanent. However, surgery does come with numerous risks and unfortunately results are not guaranteed. Injectables are safer than surgery and although the results are not permanent they can provide long term confidence and comfort with regular maintenance.

sections.heading: Hyperpigmentation Treatment London
sections.content: Book Online Reduce and remove the signs of hyperpigmentation on your skin at our award-winning professional clinic in the heart of Chelsea.

sections.heading: Skin pigmentation treatments
sections.content: In addition to being trusted Chelsea dentists , at our clinic we offer several different types of skin pigmentation treatments. These include chemical peels and prescription product treatment for hyperpigmentation and also in some cases plasma treatment. Dr Marjan Goodacre will guide you through all the potential treatments and create a treatment plan of the best procedures for you. Our pigmentation treatment can treat any kind of hyperpigmentation, and throughout our initial face consultation we can guide you through other treatment options that will complement pigmentation treatment too.

sections.heading: What is Hyperpigmentation?
sections.content: Pigmentation simply refers to the colour of your skin, while hyperpigmentation refers to an excess of melanin production, which causes dark spots or uneven patches of pigmentation to appear across the skin. Hyperpigmentation can happen to anyone, no matter their skin colour or skin texture. To create your skin’s pigmentation, cells called melanocytes create pigmentation in the form of melanin. Everyone’s skin pigmentation is on a spectrum, from those who have albinism who have almost no melanin to those who have a very dark complexion who will have a lot of melanin in their skin. Hyperpigmentation may affect both the face and the body and can show up in the form of age spots or sun spots as Solar Lentigines. Melasma and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation are two types of pigmentation that also come under the umbrella term of hyperpigmentation.

sections.heading: Who will be more affected by hyperpigmentation?
sections.content: If you have darker skin, you’re more likely to be affected by hyperpigmentation. This is because skin pigmentation is already high in those with a darker skin tone. Hyperpigmentation can occur on all skin types. Unfortunately skin pigmentation treatment can be harder to manage on those with dark skin, since the patches of increased pigmentation will emerge with a higher concentration of pigment, and as such will take longer to treat and fade.

sections.heading: What are the different types of Hyperpigmentation?
sections.content: There are many different types of Hyperpigmentation, and they can result from many different factors. The most common types of hyperpigmentation are age spots, melasma and post-inflammatory pigmentation. Age spots or lentigines are typically created due to sun damage and they normally appear on older adults. Age spots are also known as sun spots. Melasma are large patches of hyperpigmentation seen on the body and the face. Melasma are more common in women than men and are thought to be the result of a change in hormone production. Post-inflammatory pigmentation often occurs when there has been a skin injury or trauma to the skin and the skin has healed incorrectly. Post-inflammatory pigmentation is common in those with acne or eczema, but it can also be caused by cosmetic procedures such as dermabrasion, laser treatments and strong chemical peels. This is why we choose to use less aggressive treatments for hyperpigmentation to avoid causing post-inflammatory pigmentation and still achieving excellent results. Hyperpigmentation can also be caused by medication, your hormones or skin type.

sections.heading: How can Hyperpigmentation be treated?
sections.content: We’ll work with you to create a treatment plan for your pigmentation removal that works for you. There are a variety of options you can explore and we’ll recommend the best option for your skin. Dr Marjan Goodacre will examine your skin during the facial consultation and create a treatment plan based on your skin concerns. Throughout the consultation, she’ll discuss with you the risks and benefits associated with each treatment. Our treatment for pigmentation ranges from topical creams to chemical peels and sometimes plasma treatment.

sections.heading: How can Hyperpigmentation be prevented?
sections.content: If you’re concerned about hyperpigmentation increasing as you age, there are ways to reduce and prevent hyperpigmentation. We would recommend protecting your skin from the sun to reduce uneven skin tone in the future. This could include: Keeping out of the sun from the hours 10am – 4pm, when the UV rays are the strongest Minimising exposure to the sun by sitting in the shade or under an umbrella Wearing sun hats and protective clothing if you are out in the sun Even in the cooler months, using a sunscreen product every day Ensure that your skin is regularly moisturised to make sure that your skin’s lipid (fat) barrier is restored and protected from the sun’s rays Avoiding picking at scabs, spots or acne Stopping using skincare products that burn or sting as skin irritation could contribute to melasma

sections.heading: What can create hyperpigmentation of the skin?
sections.content: Hyperpigmentation can be created due to a range of factors – including sun exposure, skin conditions such as acne or eczema and hormonal changes.

sections.heading: Can hyperpigmentation be removed?
sections.content: Hyperpigmentation is not a dangerous skin condition and can be removed in a variety of ways – from non-invasive topical creams and chemical peels to plasma treatment and laser treatment.

sections.heading: Should I get an initial consultation before I start any hyperpigmentation treatment?
sections.content: We would always recommend that you see our skin specialist for a facial consultation before starting any treatment. Then we can assess what the best treatment for your skin concerns will be and we can give you guidance throughout our detailed treatment plans.

sections.heading: Is hyperpigmentation treatment painful?
sections.content: While prescription creams and chemical peels may be pain free, you will experience mild stinging, itching and later on flaking. Numbing cream is first applied for Plasma Treatment to make this procedure more comfortable.

sections.heading: How many treatment sessions are necessary?
sections.content: This varies greatly from person to person and depends on what kind of treatment you follow, the depth and age of the pigmentation you wish to treat, hormonal factors and your skin type. Some of our clients only need one treatment to treat their hyperpigmentation, others need up to six treatments.

sections.heading: Are there any side effects I should be aware of?
sections.content: The main side effects will be slight redness, tingling or stinging, itching and flaking of the skin. Our skin experts can also adjust the treatment to reduce the side effects until your skin can tolerate the treatment better.

sections.heading: Orthodontist In Chelsea, London
sections.content: Book Online Our Chelsea-based orthodontic clinic is renowned for its state-of-the-art facilities and commitment to modern orthodontics.

sections.heading: Orthodontic Clinic, London
sections.content: With a team of dedicated professionals, we ensure that every patient receives the best care tailored to their needs. Whether you’re looking for adult orthodontics or treatments for your child, our clinic is equipped to provide the highest standard of care. If you would like straight teeth and a beautiful smile, book an appointment with our Specialist Orthodontist in London. Our Specialist Orthodontist straightens teeth for both children and adults, offering a range of orthodontic treatments.

sections.heading: Why do people have orthodontic treatment?
sections.content: Orthodontic treatment will correct the positioning of the teeth and will therefore improve the function and appearance. With straighter teeth, your teeth will be easier to keep clean and so you will reduce your risk of decay or gum disease. Modern orthodontics has made it possible for people of all ages to achieve their dream smile. You are a possible candidate for orthodontic treatment if you suffer from any of the below: Overcrowding of teeth. Gaps between teeth. Asymmetrical teeth. Protruding teeth. Deep bite (upper teeth overlap and cover lower teeth too much). Reverse bite (upper teeth bite inside lower teeth). Open bite (front teeth remain apart when back teeth meet). It is important to see a Specialist Orthodontist if you would like to straighten your teeth. Our team is among one of the best orthodontists in London, led by our Specialist Orthodontist; Dr Stephanie Oiknine.

sections.heading: What are the benefits of Orthodontics?
sections.content: There are many benefits associated with orthodontics, for both adults and children. These benefits include:

sections.heading: Greater self confidence due to improved appearance of teeth and a more attractive smile.
Less chance of gum disease or decay when teeth are straightened.
Equal distribution of pressure on the jaws once the bite has been improved.
Prepares the teeth for restorative care in the future.
What is a Specialist Orthodontist?
sections.content: A Specialist Orthodontist is a fully qualified dentist who has undertaken an additional 3+ years training and examinations to specialise in orthodontics. Our Specialist Orthodontist in London is Dr. Stephanie Oiknine. Stephanie completed her specialist training in orthodontics at King’s College London and is a member of the Royal College of Surgeons. To find out if you are suitable for orthodontic treatment , you will need to book an appointment with Dr Stephanie Oiknine, our Specialist Orthodontist in London.

sections.heading: London Orthodontist
sections.content: During the orthodontics in London procedure, the orthodontist will carry out a full assessment of your teeth. If required you may also need photographs and a jaw x-ray to show the roots of your teeth. Once the orthodontist has collected all the information she will then discuss all the suitable brace options with you, how long your treatment will take and how much your treatment will cost.

sections.heading: Braces in London
sections.content: Orthodontic braces can be either fixed or removable. A brace or orthodontic appliance is used to straighten your teeth. Braces work by using gentle pressure to gradually move your teeth to the right position. Removable braces can be removed for eating, drinking and cleaning. Fixed braces are permanently attached to the teeth until the end of treatment. We understand that you don’t want it to be obvious that you’re wearing braces, which is why we specialise in using discrete braces that are difficult for others to notice. Hidden braces can be used which sit behind the teeth instead of in front of them. If you’re looking for an orthodontist in London, you’re in the right place.

sections.heading: Teeth Straightening London
sections.content: Tooth coloured ceramic braces for teeth straightening in London can be used that match the colour of your teeth or are almost completely transparent. Alternatively removable invisible braces such as Invisalign can be used which are really discrete and can be taken out. Some of the types of orthodontic dental braces we offer at our Chelsea dental clinic include Invisalign, Fixed Braces, and Lingual braces.

sections.heading: Orthodontic Treatment Procedure
sections.content: Having a brace fitted is a simple procedure. After the fitting of your brace, it’s normal to feel some discomfort around your teeth and gums as your mouth adjusts to the brace and your teeth slowly begin to move. The soreness typically disappears within a few days, until which paracetamol can be helpful. Eating and speaking with a brace can feel awkward at first, but again, this passes with time. After wearing your brace for a couple of weeks, you’ll adjust to it and the chances are you’ll forget you’re even wearing it.

sections.heading: London Specialist Orthodontist
sections.content: After your dental brace has been fitted, you will need to visit our London Specialist Orthodontist Dr Stephanie Oiknine every 4-10 weeks so the progress of the teeth straightening can be checked and adjustments to the brace can be made for further straightening. Some braces need to be worn all the time, but others only some of the time, and some need to be worn for just 6 months, whereas others need to be worn for up to 2 years. Though this may seem like a long time, keep in mind that those time-frames are for the final results, and that progress is continual from the outset. Visible improvements may take just weeks.

sections.heading: What is the best age to have a brace?
sections.content: You can have braces at any age; from as young as 7 to as old as 100. Younger children can see an orthodontist from 7 years old. There will be a mix of baby and adult teeth at this age and although it will not be possible to straighten all the adult teeth, it is important to correct certain problems and prevent more complications that will result in more complicated treatment at a later stage. The younger age is also ideal to encourage bone growth if required for jaw corrections; this will not be possible once the child has stopped growing. Adults can have braces at any age. It’s never too late to straighten your teeth. In fact, straighter teeth will help you to have a better bite and function and to help you keep your teeth cleaner and maintain healthier gums.

sections.heading: What should I expect on the first visit to the clinic?
sections.content: When you first visit us, we’ll carry out an examination and make detailed plans and notes regarding potential treatment plans. We’ll also discuss cost and payment plans with you at this time. Contact us today for access to the best London orthodontists available.

sections.heading: How much do braces cost?
sections.content: The price of braces generally varies from around £3500 to £9800. Most braces will average around £4500-£5000. The cheapest braces are generally fixed metal braces. Fixed ceramic braces are normally an upgrade of a few hundred pounds extra. Invisalign (removable clear aligner) braces can be a similar price and Lingual fixed braces are the most expensive at around £7500-£9000. The price will also depend on whether the treatment required is simple and quick or if it is complex and lengthy. The orthodontist will need to examine and assess your teeth to calculate the length of time it will take to straighten in order to calculate the exact cost. Retainers will be needed at the end of treatment and can be around £150 to £400 per arch depending on the types of retainers required.

sections.heading: How long does it take for teeth to move with braces?
sections.content: Orthodontic treatment can be completed in as short as 6 months for very minor tooth movements or it can take up to 2 years for more complex treatments. Most cases will generally take 12 to 18 months for the teeth to line up neatly. It all depends on whether the teeth were very crowded to begin with or just a little. Teeth can start to move quite quickly and with Invisalign type braces you will move to the next aligner every 1-2 weeks. With fixed braces you will need to see the orthodontist every 6 -8 weeks.

sections.heading: Which brace is best?
sections.content: All the braces can be as good as each other if in expert hands. The best thing to do is to see an orthodontist who provides treatment with all the different brace types. If the orthodontist does not use Invisalign or lingual braces for example, then they would not be able to discuss these options with you. The orthodontist can help to guide you in your decision making. Occasionally there may also be a specific tooth movement that may be more efficiently or effectively completed with a particular brace so the orthodontist can help advise if that is the case. Invisalign is removable but will need to be worn for 23 hours per day so you need to be committed for this brace option. Lingual braces will be fixed to the inside of your teeth and closer to your tongue so may take a little longer to get used to. The lingual brace will initially give you a lisp until you adapt to it being there.

sections.heading: How do I choose which brace to have?
sections.content: There are many types of braces to choose from. Cost and appearance tend to be the main deciding factors. If cost is the most important factor then traditional metal braces are most likely to be the cheapest, followed by ceramic braces and then Invisalign. Lingual braces are almost double the price of the other types. If the most important thing is appearance, then the lingual brace is the least visible, followed by Invisalign and then ceramic braces. The traditional metal braces are the least discreet. Invisalign type braces, although removable, need to be worn for 23 hours per day, so if you are unable to commit to this, then fixed braces may be a better option for you. Occasionally certain tooth movements can also influence the brace type used and an orthodontist who provides all the brace options can guide you on whether one brace can achieve certain movements better.

sections.heading: How are braces fitted and removed?
sections.content: Fixed braces comprise of small rectangular brackets (one for each tooth) and a wire. The brackets are glued to each tooth and once they are glued in the correct positions the wire is slotted into the bracket grooves. Small elastic bands are popped over each bracket keeping the wire held on tightly. At the end of treatment, the brackets are gently lifted off the tooth. The tooth is then polished to remove any remaining glue. Invisalign braces comprise of a set of clear plastic aligners which are removable. However, there will normally be a few small attachments that will be glued to a few of the teeth. The attachments are tiny clear blobs and when the aligners are not in the mouth you can barely see them. At the end of treatment the blobs are shaved back and the tooth is polished.

sections.heading: What happens after braces come off?
sections.content: Once the brace is removed it is extremely important to have retainers to hold the teeth in their new positions. Teeth will unfortunately move back if they are not held in position permanently. There are 2 main types of retainers; fixed and removable. The fixed wire retainer is a thin wire that is glued to the back of the front 6 teeth. This wire prevents rotations of the front teeth. The removable retainer is commonly a clear plastic tray which wraps around all the teeth. The removable retainer prevents larger tooth movements and changes in the shape of the arch as well as holding the front teeth in position. Both retainers are recommended best practice as the removable retainer will only be worn during the night. The fixed wire retainer will be permanently holding the front teeth secure.

sections.heading: Invisalign First in Chelsea, London
sections.content: Book Online Children between the ages of 6 to 10 years old generally have a mix of baby and adult teeth. At this stage of development, teeth can already show signs of crowding or jaw discrepancy.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: If diagnosed early, Phase 1 of Orthodontic Treatment can be provided using Invisalign First to create space for the adult teeth that need to grow in and correct issues with the jaws not lining up. Invisalign First is an important step in Interceptive Orthodontics to prevent more complicated problems from developing, making future orthodontic treatment long and complex.

sections.heading: What can I expect from Invisalign First?
sections.content: Invisalign First prepares the mouth and jaws to receive the growing adult teeth into their ideal positions. The adult teeth can then be allowed to grow and develop fully into their positions. Once the adult teeth have fully erupted, Phase 2 of Orthodontic Treatment can then take place to complete alignment. Phase 2 of Orthodontic Treatment is much simpler, quicker and less traumatic when Invisalign First has already prepared the way. Invisalign First uses aligners to help space the teeth correctly and minimise the need for orthodontics later in life. Through early intervention and a proactive approach to orthodontics, your child could enjoy straighter teeth and an aligned bite from a young age.

sections.heading: Does my child need Invisalign First?
sections.content: Orthodontic problems can easily go undetected in young children as their teeth and jaw change quickly. We recommend regular dental checkups to keep track of movements and ensure quick intervention if required. Phase 1 Invisalign treatment might be required to help in the following cases: Prevent problems with a misaligned bite Make space for adult teeth to erupt correctly Can help with oral health habits such as thumb-sucking Improve the appearance and alignment of your child’s smile Make future orthodontic treatment simpler If you are concerned about your child’s dental alignment and want to avoid extensive treatment in future, we recommend an Invisalign First consultation. We can explore the options with you and your child to determine if this is the right treatment plan.

sections.heading: What is the youngest age for Invisalign?
sections.content: Invisalign First is recommended from the age of 6 and is ideal for growing children. In addition, Invisalign aligners may be recommended to help address several alignment problems. By addressing these problems from a young age, the adult teeth have a much better chance of erupting in the correct alignment. This can help avoid crowding issues, a misaligned bite, spacing, and even narrow dental arches. After Invisalign First, your child will be familiar with the treatment and ready for Invisalign Teen. Once we have completed the initial intervention, follow up treatment is typically shorter and more successful.

sections.heading: Why parents love Invisalign First
sections.content: Invisalign First is ideal for busy parents. The unique system reduces the number of dentist visits by up to 40% compared to traditional braces. In addition, by avoiding the need for extensive treatment during their teenage years, you can further reduce the amount of time spent at the orthodontist. There are no dietary restrictions to consider, so your child can eat and drink their favourite food without concern. Children can also participate in sports and other activities without worrying about their braces getting in the way. Invisalign First also helps children to develop lifelong habits that benefit their oral health. For example, they appreciate the importance of taking care of their teeth, which translates to a lifetime of good habits. To find out if Invisalign First or Interceptive Treatment would be beneficial for your child, book an appointment today to see Dr Stephanie Oiknine, Specialist Orthodontist, at our Chelsea dental clinic .

sections.heading: What is Invisalign Full?
sections.content: With Invisalign, you can straighten your teeth and feel confident throughout treatment. With the clever computer-aided planning software, you can see your teeth fully aligned before you even start. Invisalign Full is the most comprehensive option from Invisalign. Invisalign Full allows for an unlimited number of aligners to ensure that even the most complicated cases are completed to perfection. Once your treatment is completed, you can even have further aligners to fine-tune your results to perfection. Invisalign Full can fix any alignment issues, including crowding, gaps, overbite, underbite, cross jet and more. For more complex cases, we may use attachments or precision wings to achieve a better grip on your teeth. Once the treatment is completed, you’ll have perfectly aligned teeth that are not only aesthetically pleasing but are also easier to look after.

sections.heading: How does Invisalign Full work?
sections.content: Invisalign Full uses a crystal clear, discreet, invisible, SmartTrack material for the aligners. These laser-cut aligners are designed to fit your teeth and gums perfectly, ensuring a more comfortable treatment. It all starts with a consultation. We will check your oral health to make sure you’re a suitable candidate for Invisalign. Next, we’ll use 3D scanning and AI technology to explore potential treatment outcomes. This scanning technology helps you visualise your treatment progression so that you can feel confident in the outcome.

sections.heading: Who is the ideal candidate for Invisalign Full?
sections.content: If you want to straighten your teeth without letting the whole world know you have braces, this could be the ideal treatment option for you. So many adults avoid teeth straightening because they assume they are too old or don’t want to feel self-conscious about wearing braces. Invisalign solves both problems at once by offering a nearly invisible treatment option suitable for individuals of any age. No more hiding your smile or avoiding social situations.

sections.heading: Are there any limitations with Invisalign Full?
sections.content: The Invisalign treatment plan allows you to enjoy your favourite food and drinks without any limitations. Since you remove the aligners to eat and drink, nothing is off-limits for the duration of your treatment. You can also take part in sports without worrying about your braces. However, we recommend wearing a custom fit gum shield for contact sports to protect your oral health and your aligners. And finally, you can easily care for your teeth throughout treatment. Simply remove your aligners to brush and floss twice a day, and use this opportunity to clean your aligners. For the treatment to be successful, you will need to wear the aligners for 22 hours per day. If you think you might struggle to stay on track, we can offer alternative treatment options. sections.content: Book Online The Wellington Clinic now offers Invisalign i7 in London.
